title: From scripted cutting to learned control
scope: Evidence-based progress: completed preparation is counted separately from unverified cutting and learning gates.

stages.title: Complete the scripted baseline
stages.description: A repeatable, physically separated slice is our reference.

items.text: Correct the follow-up cutting path and thumb–board clearance.
Achieve full separation through the existing material model.
Withdraw the knife and verify the slice remains supported.
items.evidence: Original run deliberately paused at checkpoint 6925. Blade has not completed withdrawal; 47 material connections remain. No supported separated slice qualified. DiSECt is a separate gated feasibility study.

items.text: Repeat the successful cut to check reliability.
Preserve the approved grip, elbow posture, and kitchen scene.
items.evidence: Approved grip, backward elbow and kitchen preserved in the mounted-robot continuation; fixed attachment remains disclosed.

stages.title: Make simulation practical for learning
stages.description: Faster runs must still meet the approved accuracy checks.

items.text: Measure where simulation time is spent.
items.evidence: Three saved current-solver profiles separate material solving, contact refresh, robot stepping and file output; material work dominates. Independent DiSECt/MPM timings and model differences recorded in solver comparison and follow-up reports.

items.text: Test faster settings against the approved accuracy limits.
items.evidence: Local material and coupled comparisons passed: maximum tomato difference 0.054 mm, knife 0.014 mm, force 0.86%. Full-cut convergence remains item 2.3.

items.text: Check accuracy over a complete cut—not only short windows.
Measure the resulting time per training episode.
Decide whether repeated simulation training is feasible.
items.evidence: Current solver measured ~9200–9600 wall seconds/sim-second in a loaded sample. Fine-mesh DiSECt candidate needs ~593 wall seconds/sim-second for bulk hold and fails settling/precision consistency. Full training episodes and a practical qualified backend remain unestablished.

stages.title: Build the learning interface
stages.description: Give the policy a small, clearly bounded job.

items.text: Define observations: relative knife pose, velocity, force, and task phase.
Define actions: small changes to downward speed and sideways motion.
Specify control frequency, units, scaling, and action limits.
Keep collision stops and force limits outside the learned policy.
Keep hidden damage information separate from policy inputs.
items.evidence: Observation allowlist and checkpoint adapter reject hidden damage/connectivity inputs. All 28 interface and episode component tests passed again.

items.text: Verify that zero learned adjustment reproduces the scripted baseline.

stages.title: Build repeatable episodes
stages.description: Every trial needs a clean start and an honest outcome.

items.text: Reset robot, knife, tomato deformation, and damage correctly.
Verify repeated resets produce consistent starting states.
Detect full separation, withdrawal, and supported-slice success.
Detect collision, excessive force, numerical failure, and timeout.
Record observations, commands, outcomes, and configuration for every trial.

stages.title: Collect demonstration data
stages.description: Successful and unsuccessful trials must stay distinguishable.

items.text: Record successful scripted cuts.
Label partial cuts and failures accurately.
Collect controlled variations in tomato position and material settings.
Split complete trials into training, validation, and held-out test sets.

stages.title: Train through imitation
stages.description: Learn from saved decisions before trying repeated simulation trials.

items.text: Train an initial policy on recorded demonstrations.
Check its predictions on held-out recordings.
Test it in simulation with action limits enforced.
Compare its cutting success and forces with the scripted baseline.

stages.title: Learn small corrections
stages.description: Scripted motion plus a bounded learned adjustment.

items.text: Combine scripted motion with bounded policy adjustments.
Define rewards that favor verified separation and controlled forces.
Check that rewards cannot be satisfied by pushing the tomato away or exploiting simulation errors.
Train only after simulation speed and reset reliability are sufficient.
Preserve a reproducible baseline for comparison.

stages.title: Evaluate and report
stages.description: Show whether learning improves the result on unseen cases.

items.text: Test unseen tomato positions and material settings.
Compare scripted, imitation, and corrected-policy performance.
Report success rate, peak force, collisions, and completion time.
Save reproducible configurations and representative failures.
Keep experimental validation and motor-work qualification pending until independently resolved.

stages.title: Separate approximate training model
stages.description: Authorized approximate blade-and-tomato task. These results do not complete the detailed reference-model or robot-learning gates above.

items.text: Keep the original setup and reference evidence unchanged.
items.evidence: 450 frozen v27 files verified unchanged; new model isolated in v28.

items.text: Cut through the full-size tomato and withdraw horizontally.
items.evidence: All eight tested bodies reached two components, withdrawal and successful terminal state.

items.text: Retain the first cut and make an intersecting second cut.
items.evidence: Four components: 817, 697, 697 and 592 particles; no physical stop.

items.text: Regenerate and test a larger tomato.
items.evidence: 20% larger shape completed a cut; time-step refinement was required.

items.text: Provide bounded actions, observations, rewards and reliable resets.
items.evidence: 25 actor observations; hidden damage kept separately for critic/diagnostics. Reset, board, force, penetration, timeout and invalid-action checks pass.

items.text: Exceed 100 complete task transitions per second.
items.evidence: 136.8 transitions/s, 25,536 transitions in186.7s, eight environments. Robot/rendering/policy inference excluded.

items.text: Show the model running live in a separate Isaac Sim view.
items.evidence: Live run observed at62.96 simulated seconds: two pieces, no stop, horizontal withdrawal complete. This is not a recorded animation.

items.text: Expand qualification to additional cutting directions.
items.evidence: 30-degree cut at80%size reached2.019N and stopped. This case has not passed; no unrestricted path/size guarantee.

items.text: Integrate the approximate tomato with the original robot, kitchen and fixed grip in a separate version.
items.evidence: Separate approximate native robot cycle passed: two pieces, horizontal withdrawal, settled support, 1.35 N peak simulated load. Fixed mount and original handle retained with the tested straight blade. Full-robot RL speed, force convergence and real-tomato validation remain pending.

latest_progress.cutting: Separate v05 float64 numerical adapter fixes lost updates and passes independent motion/reset and small-force controls. A 20ms IMEX comparison meets 0.1mm/5% accuracy limits, but the fastest valid implementation costs ~272 wall s/s versus the prospective120 budget. Numerical section3/4 verified; speed gate open/cost failed. Original checkpoint6925 and v04 failed settling preserved. No tomato contact, separation, robot integration or training.
latest_progress.learning: 218 recorded states exported as one incomplete episode; 28 component tests pass. No action labels or successful demonstrations; training disabled.

disect_feasibility.mesh_validation_scope: established prism cut surfaces and new intact FEM tomato input, not prepared tomato fracture assembly

approximate_training.numerical_accuracy: Coarse/fine complete cycles separate the same bonds, but final positions differ up to 1.54 mm and peak forces by about 46%. Not detailed-solver or real-tomato equivalence.
approximate_training.speed_scope: Complete approximate kinematic-blade task: from intact body through blade-generated separation, horizontal withdrawal, terminal reward and selective resets. Online scripted controller used instead of a learned policy. Original articulated robot, rendering and policy-network inference excluded. Identical starting cases at different batch offsets, not generalization evidence.

recommended.decision: Recommend synchronized smooth stroke for an exploratory demo: half the duration and less pre-separation RMS deformation, but higher calculated peak load than the old baseline. Do not claim lower cutting force or real-tomato validation. Fastest tested motion is close to the force stop; unsynchronized smooth cases rejected.
recommended.numerical_limit: At 0.2ms versus 0.1ms, the recommended motion has the same failure bonds and terminal success, but peak load differs by 14.3% and maximum matched-time particle position by 1.74mm. This is approximate-model screening, not precise convergence qualification.
